subject: english
question: Which sentence contains a misspelled word?

options.text: Many believed the new millennium would bring great change, but some felt embarrassed when their predictions failed.
He didn't want to embarrass himself at the start of the new millenium.
The celebration of the millennium was truly unforgettable, though it did embarrass a few politicians.
She didn't expect the event to embarrass her during the millennium gala.

solution:
The correct answer is **option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**The misspelled word is 'millenium'.**

__
 
• **The correct spelling would be 'millennium'.**
 
• The word '**millennium**' is a **noun** which means 'a period of one thousand years'. **(सहस्त्राब्दी)**
 
 
• **For Example -** 
 
• The new millennium was celebrated with great enthusiasm across the globe.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer would be** 'millenium'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Let's understand the meanings of the other marked words in the sentence - **

 
• **Embarrass -** to cause someone to feel awkward, self-conscious, or ashamed **(शर्मिंदा करना)**
 
• **Believed - **to accept something as true or feel sure of the truth **(विश्वास करना)**
 
• **Predictions -** a statement about what will happen in the future **(भविष्यवाणी)**
